claims.text: risk-register-example.md lines 9-16, column Cách xử lý: R1, R2, R5 'Giảm' (reduce); R3 'Tránh' (avoid: partial refunds out of scope); R4 'Chuyển' (transfer to customer care, who can reach customers and do this daily); R6 'Chấp nhận' (accept, with reason).

R1 response: try the gateway's test environment in the first week of Sprint 15, before writing the job that sends requests. R2 response: ask the provider in week one; if no idempotency key, the job asks refund status before each resend.
R6 accepted with reason: customers still see the refund status in the app; making email faster costs more than the harm; owner Tester; sign: customers complain about missing email.
Owners (Người theo dõi) are roles: integration developer (R1, R2), product owner (R3, R5), head of customer care (R4), tester (R6); every row has a warning sign (Dấu hiệu).
Lines 24-25: each risk has exactly one person watching its sign; when the sign appears that person reports at the daily, not waiting for sprint planning.

Four common responses: avoid (change the plan), reduce (likelihood or impact), transfer (to someone better placed), accept (no work to lower it; watch, at most agree what to do if it happens); accepting is valid when reducing costs more than the harm, if written with its reason.
One owner per risk, the person best placed to see the sign early; a risk everyone owns is a risk nobody checks; a response is concrete work with a when, not a wish like 'be careful'.
